lines.text: Left at the next corner.
Right at the next corner.
Left here. Left!
Right here, take the right!
Keep left.
Keep right.
Stay on this one, straight ahead.
You passed it. Turn around.
Okay, wrong turn. Hold on, I'm finding you another way.
It's right up ahead.
It's on your left.
It's on your right.
That's the place. Go get it.
You got it? Nice. Now get it back here before it gets out.
That's one. Bring the trap home, the containment unit is waiting.
Did it slime you? Do not get that in the car.
The city is gonna bill us for that.
Was that a fire hydrant?
The city paid. Minus the damage. Again.
Payment's in. You broke less stuff this time. Barely.
Okay, head back to the Firehouse. I'll talk you in.
You're home. Back it in, and mind the door this time.
Ecto-1, radio check. You're on. Suit up when you get there.
Quiet night. Don't get used to it.
Ecto-1, come in. We got one. The hot dog stand on North Moore and Varick, right around the corner. Something green is eating everything on the cart. Then the cart.
Loading dock on Washington and Beach, in Tribeca. The night guard says something with horns is chewing on the crates. He sounded sober.
Ecto-1, we got a call. Golden Dragon on Mott and Canal. Something is eating the whole kitchen, and the owner wants to know who's paying for the duck.
Ecto-1, come in. World Trade Center plaza, Church and Vesey. Security says there's a pack of little glowing things on the fountain. A lot of them.
Guys, Trinity Church, Broadway and Wall. The organist says the graveyard is, quote, getting up. I didn't ask.
Ecto-1, Battery pier, all the way down at the tip. A cab drove off the pier. The driver's still in it. He's been dead since nineteen forty.
South Street Seaport, South and Fulton. Something is eating the fish market, and the fish market is not happy.
Ecto-1, Greene and Spring, the old cast iron lofts. An artist says his sculptures are howling. He thinks it's a ghost, I think it's the sculptures.
Canal Street subway, Canal and Seventh Avenue South. The token booth lady says the trains are coming out of the tunnel with nobody driving.
Ecto-1, Washington Square, by the arch. Something big and black with red eyes is chasing the chess players. They want their money back.
Herald Square, Broadway and Thirty-Fourth. A taxi with no driver keeps doing laps around the square. Honking. At night.
Ecto-1, come in. Library steps, Fifth Avenue and Forty-Second. There's an old lady floating between the lions, telling people to be quiet.
We got one inside the New York Public Library, the main reading room. Books flying off the shelves. The librarian is very upset, and I mean the live one.
Ecto-1, Times Square, Broadway and Seventh. Half the city is out there watching something eat a hot dog truck. Try not to be on TV.
Sedgewick Hotel, Madison and Forty-Third. Something green is eating the whole banquet in the ballroom. The manager says, and I quote, discretion.
Ecto-1, Columbus Circle. A cab with no driver is going around and around the statue. The other cabs are getting jealous.
Fifty-Five Central Park West. Tenants say there's a dog on the roof. A big dog. With horns. Doorman quit an hour ago.
Ecto-1, Tavern on the Green, Central Park West and Sixty-Seventh. Something is terrorizing the guests through the windows. Reservations are canceled.
Central Park, the pond by Fifth Avenue. Joggers see little glowing things skimming over the water. Lots of little glowing things.
Ecto-1, Bethesda Fountain in the middle of the park. The angel on the fountain is screaming. Statues aren't supposed to do that, right?
